title: Natural generic scalar comparison for all-continuous lisse coefficients
statement:
Let $X$ be a nonempty normal integral locally Noetherian scheme [def-pc-integral-scheme, pqf-def-locnoeth], where normal means that every local ring is an integrally closed domain [def-weil-pbc-normal-ring]. Write $k=\mathcal O_{X,\eta}$ for its function field, choose a separable closure $k^s/k$ [def-pd-separable-closure], and put $G_k=\operatorname{Aut}_k(k^s)$ with its profinite Krull topology. For any nonarchimedean normed field $A$ (a field with a multiplicative absolute value satisfying $|a+b|\leq\max(|a|,|b|)$), put $R_{A,T}=p_T^*\underline A$, where $\underline A(S)=C(S,A)$ for profinite $S$ [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring, sk-def-sfb-pulled-back-coefficients]. All module objects and lisse modules are those of [sk-def-sfb-module-objects, def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module] on the small pro-etale site [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Use all continuous functions with the norm topology. Let $B$ be another nonarchimedean normed field and $\varphi:A\hookrightarrow B$ a continuous field homomorphism. Along postcomposition by $\varphi$ and pullback [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], use ordinary internal scalar extension [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. For every lisse $R_{A,X}$-module $L$, the module
$$L_B=R_{B,X}\otimes_{R_{A,X}}L$$
is lisse of the same rank, and there is a canonical isomorphism, natural in $L$,
$$B\otimes_A V_A(L)\xrightarrow{\sim} V_B(L_B),\qquad b\otimes v\longmapsto b\,v_B,$$
where $V_A(L)=\Gamma((\operatorname{Spec}k^s)_{\mathrm{proet}},L|_{k^s})$ and $v_B$ is the image under the scalar-extension unit. In bases, the transition matrices and generic Galois descent matrices of $L_B$ are the entrywise images under $\varphi$ of those of $L$. Under the displayed isomorphism the $G_k$-action is $g(b\otimes v)=b\otimes\sigma_L(g)v$, with the cocycle convention of [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates]. A morphism with generic matrix $T$ extends to the matrix $\varphi_*(T)$, and the displayed comparison commutes with every such morphism. If $X$ is quasi-compact and the two generic actions factor through the induced surjection $q:G_k\to\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)$ [def-galois-fibre-functor], the same comparison intertwines those factored actions, and also their transports by any one fixed topological isomorphism $\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar\eta)\cong\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$. These assertions include rank zero and do not restrict continuous $B$-valued functions to functions valued in a finite subextension.

source.place: Agent entrywise tensor/descend comparison in the framework of Lemma 7.4.7, pp. 70–71; all-continuous norm topology, not the colimit topology of Example 7.1.7.

proof.text: For a scheme morphism $h:T\to X$, abelian inverse image preserves colimits [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] and tensor products [lem-sfb-finite-upper-star-tensor]. Apply it to the defining pair of arrows and coequalizer for $R_{B,X}\otimes_{R_{A,X}}L$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. The monoidal natural coefficient identifications [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp] identify that pair with the defining pair for $R_{B,T}\otimes_{R_{A,T}}h^*L$: the two arrows respectively multiply the coefficient and act on the module. Their coequalizers are therefore canonically isomorphic. The comparison carries the generalized balanced tensor to the corresponding tensor and the unit $m\mapsto1\otimes m$ to that same unit. This also applies to a trivializing slice via its scheme inverse image, which is slice restriction [lem-sfb-coefficient-sections-localization]. These are coequalizers of sheaves; no assertion about sections commuting with arbitrary tensor products is used.

source.place: Agent coequalizer calculation for ordinary tensor, in the framework of Lemma 7.4.7, p. 70.

proof.text: Choose the pro-etale slice trivializations $L|_{U_i}\cong R_{A,U_i}^{\oplus r_i}$ supplied by [def-sfb-lisse-coefficient-module]. Step 1 and [lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension] give $L_B|_{U_i}\cong R_{B,U_i}^{\oplus r_i}$. Thus the same cover proves lisseness, preserving every local rank. On an overlap the same free-matrix lemma sends a transition matrix $(a_{uv})$ to its image under the coefficient map, section by section. By [def-sfb-continuous-map-condensed-ring-map], that map is postcomposition with $\varphi$ and pullback. A transition inverse maps to its inverse, since a ring map respects matrix products, so these are the transition maps of the given tensor sheaf. This includes rank zero.

source.place: Agent local-basis calculation, Lemma 7.4.7 framework, p. 70.

proof.text: Put $h:\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to X$. Pulling back the trivializations of $L$ makes $h^*L$ lisse: inverse image preserves the covering [det-pe-topos-functoriality-inverse-image] and sends the coefficient ring to $R_{A,k^s}$ [sk-def-sfb-pullback-from-point-comp]. By [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates], $h^*L\cong R_{A,k^s}^{\oplus n}$ and its sections are $A^n$, since $\Gamma(\operatorname{Spec}k^s,R_{A,k^s})=A$ [lem-sfb-galois-continuous-section-naturality]. Step 1 and the free-matrix lemma [lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension] identify $h^*L_B$ with $R_{B,k^s}^{\oplus n}$, whose sections are $B^n$ by the same section identification for $B$. The balanced map $b\otimes v\mapsto b\,v_B$ thus becomes $B\otimes_A A^n\to B^n$, $b\otimes(a_j)\mapsto(b\varphi(a_j))$. Its inverse is $(b_j)\mapsto\sum_j b_j\otimes e_j$, and the balancing relation checks both composites. The map was defined by the coefficient unit before choosing a basis, so it is canonical.

source.place: Agent generic finite-basis calculation, Lemma 7.4.7 framework, p. 70.

proof.text: Let $u:L\to M$ have generic matrix $T=(t_{ij})$ in chosen generic bases. The free-matrix lemma [lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension] gives matrix $\varphi_*(T)$ after extension. For the comparison $\theta$ of step 3, both paths of its naturality square send $b\otimes v$ to $b\,(u(v))_B$: indeed $u_B(1\otimes v)=1\otimes u(v)$ by the functorial coequalizer construction [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]. Pure tensors generate the ordinary vector-space tensor, proving naturality. In particular the equality holds for changes of generic bases; the coordinate computations impose no choices on $\theta$.

source.place: Agent naturality calculation on pure tensors, Lemma 7.4.7 framework, p. 70.

proof.text: Restrict $L$ first to $\operatorname{Spec}k$ and use the cover $\operatorname{Spec}k^s\to\operatorname{Spec}k$. By [lem-sfb-field-separable-cech-coordinates] its pullback to $\operatorname{Spec}k^s$ is free and $\Gamma(W_1,R_A)=C(G_k,A)$ for $W_1=(\operatorname{Spec}k^s)^2_{/k}$; the descent isomorphism between the two face pullbacks is an automorphism of $R_A^{\oplus n}$ on the slice over $W_1$, hence by [lem-sfb-ringed-site-free-matrix-scalar-extension] an invertible matrix $c$ over $C(G_k,A)$, with $c(gh)=c(g)c(h)$ in the specified convention by the cocycle condition on $W_2$. By step 1 the face pullbacks of $L_B$ are the scalar extensions of those of $L$, and its descent isomorphism is the functorial extension of that of $L$ [sk-def-sfb-change-of-scalars]; the free-matrix lemma and that node's coefficient-natural Cech coordinates identify its matrix with $\varphi\circ c$ over $C(G_k,B)$. The resulting action is therefore entrywise $\varphi(c(g))$, and is continuous. The face-compatible coordinates have trivial action on the constant coefficients [lem-sfb-galois-continuous-section-naturality], so $g$ fixes $b\in B$. In the basis of step 3, matrix multiplication now gives $\theta(b\otimes\sigma_L(g)v)=\sigma_{L_B}(g)\theta(b\otimes v)$, proving exactly $g(b\otimes v)=b\otimes\sigma_L(g)v$. These are the full continuous-function rings in the cited nodes.

source.place: Agent coefficient-natural descent calculation with the field Cech convention; Lemma 7.4.7 framework, pp. 70–71.

proof.text: Finally assume both actions factor through the stipulated surjection $q:G_k\to\Pi$. Given $\gamma\in\Pi$, choose $g$ with $q(g)=\gamma$ and apply step 5. Factorization makes the equality independent of the lift, proving $\Pi$-equivariance. For the one fixed topological isomorphism $a:\Pi\to\pi_1^{\mathrm{et}}(X,\bar x)$, its transported action of $\delta$ is the old action of $a^{-1}(\delta)$; substitute this element into that equality. For $n=0$, step 3 has the unique map $0\to0$ and its empty-sum inverse, and every matrix and equivariance identity still holds. Neither tensor computation restricts continuous functions to finite subextensions.

source.place: Elementary descent of an intertwining identity along a surjection and precomposition by a fixed isomorphism.

proof_origin.place: Explicit coequalizer and matrix argument in the framework of Lemma 7.4.7, pp. 70–71; not an appeal to its local-field classification for arbitrary normed fields.
